assignments.brief_reason: Tone/antagonistic/foul language triggers deletion, fitting the profanity/adjacent moderation exception style.
Explicit/implicit threats are removed while other speech is protected.
Ad hominem attacks are singled out for removal, consistent with removing toxic/abusive content.
Removes statements wishing death and heavy profanity—removed for highly toxic/offensive threats/vulgarity.
Nasty language is disallowed as unhealthy/toxic, aligning with the toxicity-removal theme.
Incitement of violence against group/individual is treated as disqualifying.
Main cues are vulgar/offensive/direct attacks (with some borderline/context), matching toxicity filtering.
Focus is on hearing both sides rather than explicitly equal standards across viewpoints.
Prioritizes forward discussion over personal attacks; not clearly captured by the provided threat/toxicity/free-speech themes.
General norm against aggression; does not map cleanly to specific removal exceptions in the themes.
Removes rude/hurtful content lacking real claims; resembles toxicity/low-substance deletion.
Prohibits cussing as part of quality/intelligent debate, which aligns with profanity/toxicity removal.
Mentions removal for encroaching on hate speech; closest match is threat/toxicity exceptions but hate-speech isn’t explicitly in themes.
Vulgar language leads to immediate rejection while discussion intent may still be considered.
Decision driven by being horrified/lack of knowledge, not a specific moderation exception cue.
Pair-comparison via underlying attitude; not a moderation-rule/toxicity/violence exception.
Same-event vs different-events negatively perceived by opponents—pair-comparison strategy not in given moderation themes.
Distinguishes targeting groups vs individuals; not directly tied to threat/toxicity removal criteria in the themes.
Keeps speech unless it incites violence against specific people, which should be deleted.
Abusive language is rejected even while other expression rights are respected.
